Stage 01 mapped supplied control claims without promoting them to implemented or tested status.
Stage 01 mapped supplied product and security requirements to modeled system records.

scope.description: Specification-only composed deep threat model of The Daily Dread browser application and private HTTP/JSON API. Web is primary; API is a bounded secondary. Boundary ownership is explicit and shared contributors are retained.
in_scope: Browser application, application origin, OIDC login, server-side session and bearer-token admission
Private API resource, operation and property authorization
Report views and PDF, CSV and JSON exports
Durable asynchronous ingestion, repository analysis, correction, delivery and recovery reached through web/API operations
GitHub, source, identity, AI and notification adapters and their responses
PostgreSQL persistence, audit history and security-event obligations
Rendering of publisher text, evidence, company notes, identifiers and errors
out_of_scope: Implementation defects, runtime behavior and deployment claims
Public APIs, public feeds, native mobile clients and native password or recovery flows
Inbound notification-provider callbacks and public webhooks, which FR-10.13 excludes
User file uploads and upload preview/download flows, which the release does not define
Third-party browser code and service workers, which the specifications exclude from the proposed client
Optional method executions and risk scoring without a supplied rubric
objectives: Prevent unauthorized company, resource, function and property access across UI, API, exports and jobs
Preserve intended browser request authority, session transitions and current roles
Keep provider and repository content inert, bounded and unable to direct execution
Prevent private evidence, credentials and company context from crossing unapproved output or provider boundaries
Preserve durable work identity, revocation, correction and failure semantics without duplicate effects
Keep audit and security-event claims distinct from emission, persistence, detection and alert delivery
assumptions: The five supplied specifications describe the intended release, not implemented behavior.
The single-company deployment still requires explicit company context at every protected use case.
Proposed architecture and control text grounds design hypotheses but is not effectiveness evidence.
limitations: No implementation, tests, deployment configuration, live provider data or runtime observations exist or were inspected.
Working-tree cleanliness was not checked because configured clean/process filters made protected status unavailable under the runbook.
Only the five caller-named project documents were inspected; no optional methods or technology pack ran.
Open evidence and decision gaps make this artifact partial; they are not proof of vulnerabilities.

evidence.statement: The release is a private company web application and private API; public feeds, third-party API integrations, native mobile applications and native password authentication are excluded.
UI and private API share company scope and workflows; OIDC roles distinguish user, admin and owner-scoped personal settings, while all admitted users may read company repository analysis.
evidence.limitations: No concrete route or policy matrix is supplied.

evidence.statement: Admin repository operations feed durable news/advisory-triggered work with bounded concurrency, retained event identity, revocation behavior and visible progress/failure states.
Authorized PDF, CSV and JSON exports preserve evidence, status, provenance and gaps; failures cannot overwrite prior findings with a clean result.
Sources, delivery providers and GitHub issues are external boundaries; no inbound notification callback or public webhook is required.
evidence.limitations: Provider response schemas are not enumerated.

evidence.statement: The repository is specification-only. One Node.js/Fastify service and PostgreSQL database are confirmed core choices; the native browser client and HTTP/JSON API are proposed and share Fastify gates.
The architecture assigns logical component ownership and TB-1 through TB-10 across clients, identity, providers, transient/retained data, PostgreSQL, outputs and restricted operations.
evidence.limitations: Component statuses do not claim implementation or tests.

evidence.statement: Protected use cases require trusted context and authorization before side effects; browser login/session, CSRF/origin, role freshness, mixed-credential rejection and fresh-auth rules are specified.
evidence.limitations: Required controls are not implemented or verified.

evidence.statement: HTTP, SQL, outbound requests, parsing, repository inspection, secrets and AI egress have explicit validation, scoping, destination, budget and evidence rules.
evidence.limitations: Required controls are not effectiveness observations.

evidence.statement: Rendering is inert and restricted, private responses are no-store, downloads stay authenticated, output is context-safe, and durable jobs revalidate authority and fence stale work.
evidence.limitations: No runtime header, browser or worker observations exist.

evidence.statement: Security verification is future work and OD-001 through OD-005 leave security-event destinations, retention, personal-data policy, durability and AI digest representation unresolved.
evidence.limitations: Open decisions have no assigned owner in the evidence.

evidence.statement: The closed security-event contract and ledger are specification mappings only; rows are missing, unavailable-signal or not-applicable, and runtime verification is not run.
evidence.limitations: No event is covered by implementation evidence.

evidence.statement: Design rules expose uncertainty, identity/role, session loss, confirmation tiers, safe errors, external-link hosts, bidi controls and redaction locations; DQ-8 leaves some confirmation targets unresolved.
Nothing is implemented yet; missing details are evidence gaps rather than code-level findings.
evidence.limitations: Caller statement about review scope and evidence state.

flows.rationale: Specified ordering is not an implementation observation.

flows.rationale: Destination and parser controls are required but unverified.

flows.rationale: Provider permissions and inspection code are absent.

flows.rationale: PostgreSQL work rows and wake-ups are proposed.

flows.rationale: Matching policies are specified but not executed.

flows.rationale: Post-revocation retrieval and result lifetime are not allocated.

entry_points.description: Internal durable-work consumer using service/job context and current authority checks.

dependencies.rationale: Unavailable permissions become visible coverage gaps.

dependencies.rationale: Failures must remain visible and cannot imply safety.

dependencies.rationale: Concrete schema, isolation and recovery behavior are unimplemented.

Optional AI advice depends on approved provider terms, model/configuration and safe final-byte projection; local assessment remains available without it.
dependencies.rationale: Activation and audit representation may block external use.

threats.scenario: A party able to induce an authenticated browser request causes a cookie-authenticated mutation that the user did not intend if a state-changing route lacks effective session-bound CSRF and configured-origin enforcement.
threats.objective: Preserve intended browser authority for mutations.
prerequisites: The target operation accepts ambient browser session authority.
The attacker can cause the authenticated browser to submit the operation.
The concrete route omits or misapplies the required CSRF/origin checks.
actor_assumptions: Can influence a user's browser to make a request but does not possess the session secret.
Knows or can infer the state-changing operation and accepted fields.
threats.confidence_rationale: The browser mutation surface and required countercontrol are explicit, but no route inventory or implementation exists. C-WEB-REQUEST would defeat the scenario if implemented for every mutation; route-level enforcement evidence would decide it.

threats.scenario: A session or cached authorization remains usable after logout, role removal, issuer/mapping change or privilege transition, allowing stale access or leaving private company data visible after authority is lost.
threats.objective: Make identity, role and displayed private state follow current authority transitions.
prerequisites: A valid session or displayed private response predates an authority transition.
Session/configuration revision or role freshness is not rechecked within the specified bound, or old browser state is not cleared.
The stale context can reach a protected read or operation.
actor_assumptions: Previously held valid user or admin authority.
Can replay an old session context or continue using an already open browser view.
threats.confidence_rationale: The specifications explicitly require invalidation, bounded freshness and UI clearing, which are strong counterclaims but not implementation evidence. Session-transition and browser-storage tests would decide the scenario.

threats.scenario: A valid user changes an object identifier, invokes an admin function through an alternate API route, or supplies/receives unauthorized properties to alter another user's personal settings or privileged shared state.
threats.objective: Preserve object, function, property, personal-owner and admin authorization across UI and API routes.
prerequisites: The caller has valid authentication but lacks the required owner or admin permission.
An alternate identifier, function or property reaches a use case.
The use case relies on submitted ownership/role data or an unscoped lookup/projection.
actor_assumptions: Is an admitted company user able to call private API operations.
Can modify identifiers, requested functions or writable/readable properties.
threats.confidence_rationale: The differentiated user/admin and personal-owner model makes this scenario concrete. C-AUTHZ and C-VALIDATION are explicit countercontrols; the missing per-operation matrix and implementation keep it a hypothesis.

threats.scenario: An export selected while access was valid is generated or retrieved after role loss, archive, source-use restriction or report-scope change, or a caller retrieves another export by changing a job/result identifier.
threats.objective: Keep export creation, retained result and download authority current and resource-bound.
prerequisites: Export selection and execution or retrieval occur at different times.
Authority or source-use state changes, or the result identifier is caller-influenced.
The worker/download path trusts enqueue-time authority or identifier possession without current scoped authorization.
actor_assumptions: Can create or observe an export job/result identifier while authorized, or can alter a candidate identifier.
Later lacks current permission for the report or retained content.
threats.confidence_rationale: Delayed export and authenticated download are explicit flows, while their lifecycle allocation is an acknowledged topology gap. C-AUTHZ, C-OUTPUT and C-JOBS are countercontrols; an end-to-end export authority contract and tests would decide it.

threats.scenario: Publisher text, company or vendor names, company notes, file/evidence excerpts or model output is interpreted as active browser content in another user's or administrator's view.
threats.objective: Render every untrusted content source inertly while preserving the restricted note format.
prerequisites: Attacker-influenced content reaches a rendered view.
A renderer, preview or later transformation bypasses the shared inert/restricted representation.
The receiving browser executes or applies active content in the application origin.
actor_assumptions: Can influence an ingested source, proposed vendor/company-visible string, company note through an authorized admin account, repository evidence or model output.
Targets a user or admin who views the stored content.
threats.confidence_rationale: Multiple specified untrusted text sources cross into privileged views. C-OUTPUT and C-UNTRUSTED-DATA explicitly counter the scenario, but no renderer or transformation evidence exists.

threats.scenario: A private report, repository excerpt or company context is reused from a shared cache or remains in browser storage after signout/role loss and is exposed to a later unauthorized recipient.
threats.objective: Prevent private response reuse across recipients and clear private client state after authority loss.
prerequisites: A private response or derived view is cached or persisted beyond the authorized context.
A later recipient lacks the original authority but can receive or display the stored response.
No-store, browser-storage prohibition or session-loss clearing is absent or ineffective.
actor_assumptions: Can access the same intermediary cache or browser profile after the authorized session.
Does not otherwise have permission to the private content.
threats.confidence_rationale: Private responses and explicit no-store/browser-clearing requirements ground the scenario. Those requirements are strong counterevidence at design level; runtime header and storage observations are missing.

threats.scenario: An admin-configured source/provider/destination URL or a redirect causes an outbound adapter to connect to an unapproved internal, metadata, alternate-origin or attacker-controlled destination.
threats.objective: Constrain every outbound connection to its purpose-specific approved destination and address policy.
prerequisites: A configurable URL, provider discovery result or redirect influences an outbound destination.
Socket-level address and redirect validation is missing, bypassed or weaker on retry.
The service network can reach a prohibited target or forwards credentials/payload to it.
actor_assumptions: Can influence an admin-configured integration/source value, source redirect or provider response.
Knows a target reachable from the service network.
threats.confidence_rationale: Configurable retrieval and provider adapters make the boundary concrete. C-EGRESS is unusually detailed counterevidence, but it is only a required control without transport evidence.

threats.scenario: A source, AI or delivery-provider response field is trusted as business authority, allowing untrusted data or an acknowledgment to alter finding, delivery, configuration or workflow state beyond its defined meaning.
threats.objective: Keep external response data typed, bounded and non-authoritative except through an explicit local policy transition.
prerequisites: An external response contains attacker/provider-influenced fields.
The adapter passes fields beyond its validated schema or semantic contract.
A downstream owner treats the response as permission, human readership, definite evidence or authorization to change business state.
actor_assumptions: Controls or can influence an external payload or compromised provider response.
Cannot directly call the internal state transition but can shape the response consumed by it.
threats.confidence_rationale: Provider responses feed several business flows and G-005 explicitly records missing field/authority allocation. C-VALIDATION, C-UNTRUSTED-DATA and C-JOBS are countercontrols; adapter contracts would decide it.

threats.scenario: A queued or running job performs a repository read, issue write, notification, AI request or result commit after repository access, source rights, recipient authority or resource state was revoked, or after its lease was superseded.
threats.objective: Make delayed work obey current authority and fencing at every effect and commit.
prerequisites: Work is admitted before an authority/resource-state change or lease expiry.
The worker trusts queued context or stale attempt state.
No current authorization/resource-state check and fencing token protects the external effect or commit.
actor_assumptions: Can trigger or wait for a legitimate delayed workflow, or cause revocation/archive while it is pending.
May control a stale worker attempt or exploit timing without direct database authority.
threats.confidence_rationale: The architecture explicitly contains delayed work and revocation/archive transitions. C-JOBS and C-AUTHZ directly counter the scenario, but no implementation or recovery evidence exists.

threats.scenario: A timeout, crash or unknown provider outcome is blindly retried, creating duplicate notifications, issue updates, external AI charges or other effects, or recording a false success/failure state.
threats.objective: Preserve one logical operation across retries and distinguish unknown, provider acceptance and human outcome.
prerequisites: An external effect may have occurred but its result is unknown.
A retry is issued without stable effect identity, provider reconciliation or effect-specific idempotency.
The provider or local owner does not safely deduplicate the attempt.
actor_assumptions: Can induce timeout, connection loss, crash or delayed provider response.
Benefits from duplicate or inconsistent external effects but need not compromise provider credentials.
threats.confidence_rationale: The requirements explicitly distinguish unknown outcomes and demand reconciliation, demonstrating the relevant invariant. C-JOBS is counterevidence only at specification level; restart and provider-reconciliation tests would decide it.

threats.scenario: Large, deeply nested, highly expanded or numerous HTTP/source/repository/export inputs exhaust event-loop, worker, memory, database, disk or provider capacity and delay interactive or durable work.
threats.objective: Maintain bounded availability and visible backlog under untrusted and high-volume work.
prerequisites: An actor or provider can supply data or request work near an exposed processing boundary.
One or more byte, depth, expansion, concurrency, time, queue or temporary-storage limits is absent or ineffective.
Shared capacity is consumed before cancellation, shedding or bounded failure.
actor_assumptions: Can make authorized API/export requests or influence source/repository content.
Can repeat work within whatever admission limits exist.
threats.confidence_rationale: High-volume repository/source/export processing and conservative budgets are specified, making availability exposure concrete. C-VALIDATION, C-UNTRUSTED-DATA and C-EGRESS would constrain it; no load or adversarial parser evidence exists.

threats.scenario: Private repository/company identifiers or sensitive snippets cross the AI boundary, or returned model evidence identifiers resolve outside the authorized assessment and contaminate a finding.
threats.objective: Keep AI egress minimized and local evidence authority assessment-scoped.
prerequisites: An assessment invokes the optional external AI provider.
Final serialized bytes bypass or outgrow the allowlisted projection, or returned references are accepted without local scoped resolution.
The result is persisted, displayed or delivered as supported advice/evidence.
actor_assumptions: Can influence repository/source/model text or provider response.
May attempt to include private identifiers or invented/cross-assessment evidence references.
threats.confidence_rationale: The specifications explicitly call out final-byte gating, placeholders and scoped reference resolution, which makes both failure modes concrete and supplies countercontrols. Captured-byte and cross-assessment tests are absent; AI digest auditing is blocked.

threats.scenario: A notification, shared Slack message or public GitHub issue is sent to an unauthorized destination or includes private company/repository evidence because current destination access, source rights or public-evidence classification is not rechecked.
threats.objective: Prevent external output from disclosing private or rights-restricted information.
prerequisites: A finding, correction or report is eligible for external delivery.
Destination authority, recipient access, source rights or public/private classification changes or is evaluated incorrectly.
The output projection includes fields not permitted for that channel/destination.
actor_assumptions: Can influence destination/routing configuration, report content or resource lifecycle, or is a former recipient.
Can observe the external channel or public issue.
threats.confidence_rationale: The product explicitly supports private data, shared Slack and public issue output, and requires immediate rechecks. C-OUTPUT, C-AUTHZ and C-JOBS are countercontrols, but no channel-specific projection or delivery evidence exists.

threats.scenario: A denied, failed, rolled-back or AI-egress action cannot be durably recorded, independently observed or represented under the closed event schema, leaving administrators unable to investigate or distinguish silence from health.
threats.objective: Preserve trustworthy accountability and bounded detection for security-relevant actions and pipeline failure.
prerequisites: A required event occurs outside the atomic administrative transaction, or requires the unresolved AI digest field.
No approved durable path/destination/consumer or independent silence monitor is available.
Ordinary telemetry emission fails, drops or cannot represent the obligation.
actor_assumptions: Can trigger a denied/failed/rolled-back security-relevant action or exploit an operational outage.
Benefits from reduced investigation evidence without needing to alter the business record.
threats.confidence_rationale: OD-001 through OD-005 explicitly acknowledge unresolved representation, destination and durability obligations; this is a supported design gap, not a claim that events are currently lost. C-AUDIT preserves the intended contract but cannot close the decisions.

threats.scenario: Concurrent or retried privileged edits overwrite a newer repository/source/connector/OIDC configuration, activate stale authority, or commit a mutation without the matching audit/configuration revision.
threats.objective: Preserve privileged configuration invariants and accountability under concurrency and retry.
prerequisites: Two administrators or a retry operate on the same configuration/resource revision.
The mutation does not bind authorization and expected revision in one scoped transaction or equivalent lock/constraint.
A stale write can become active or audit/work intent does not commit atomically with it.
actor_assumptions: Has legitimate admin access or can replay an admin operation after an uncertain response.
Can create a concurrent update but does not require database privileges.
threats.confidence_rationale: The API defines 409 conflicts and security rules require version/locking and atomic audit, so the invariant is concrete. No operation-specific commitment/precondition matrix or transaction implementation exists.

threats.scenario: Malformed, ambiguous, contradictory or incomplete source/repository evidence is accepted as a definite match or clean result, corrupting findings and suppressing needed follow-up.
threats.objective: Preserve evidence integrity and explicit uncertainty in exposure determinations.
prerequisites: Untrusted evidence is malformed, ambiguous, unsupported, truncated or contradictory.
Validation/comparison/coverage policy silently normalizes or drops the uncertainty.
The assessment emits a definite exposure or clean result without the required evidence.
actor_assumptions: Can influence a source or repository artifact, or relies on naturally incomplete provider evidence.
Benefits from a false clean, false definite match or obscured coverage gap.
threats.confidence_rationale: The product requirements repeatedly forbid unsupported definite or clean results, demonstrating a central integrity invariant. C-UNTRUSTED-DATA and the supplied requirements counter it; parser/comparator implementation evidence is absent.

threats.scenario: Restoring database/configuration state reactivates obsolete sessions, queued effects or connector credentials before current destinations, rights and keys are revalidated.
threats.objective: Keep restored installations quarantined until authority and external effects are explicitly re-established.
prerequisites: A backup restores business state, session/work records and encrypted connector references.
Startup resumes service, jobs or connectors without the specified quarantine gate.
Old sessions, destinations, access grants or credentials are no longer authorized.
actor_assumptions: Can influence restore sequencing or exploit a restored stale session/effect.
May be a former authorized recipient or principal rather than a database administrator.
threats.confidence_rationale: Restore quarantine is a specified control and ledger subject, so the transition is concrete. No restore implementation or exercise exists; C-AUTHN, C-SECRETS-AI, C-JOBS and C-AUDIT would jointly defeat it.

controls.description: OIDC code/PKCE/state/nonce validation, issuer/audience/signature/time binding, opaque server-side sessions, rotation, expiry and mixed-credential rejection are required.
controls.limitations: Required by SEC-2; not implemented or tested.

controls.description: Every UI, API, export and job use case must receive trusted context, bind company/owner/object/operation and authorize before disclosure, mutation or side effects.
controls.limitations: No concrete policy matrix or implementation evidence.

controls.description: Cookie-authenticated mutations require session-bound CSRF evidence and configured-origin validation; GET/HEAD do not change business state except the validated OIDC callback.
controls.limitations: Exact route mapping and runtime enforcement are absent.

controls.description: Routes must declare authentication, media, byte and pagination bounds, reject unknown/duplicate/invalid fields and use scoped parameterized database access.
controls.limitations: Registered schemas, parsers and SQL do not yet exist.

controls.description: Integration adapters enforce purpose-specific HTTPS destinations, socket-level address validation, redirect revalidation, credentials scope and cumulative byte/time budgets.
controls.limitations: No transport implementation or socket-level test evidence.

controls.description: Repository/source/provider/model content stays data, cannot select execution capabilities, is parsed under finite budgets and crosses retention only after validation/redaction.
controls.limitations: No parsers, workers or adversarial tests exist.

controls.description: Credentials stay behind a restricted adapter and AI receives only a final validated allowlisted projection without private identifiers or tools; returned references remain assessment-scoped.
controls.limitations: No captured-byte test exists and audit digest representation is unresolved.

controls.description: One authorized projection drives inert browser/API/export/message output, restricted notes, no-store private responses, authenticated downloads and context-specific CSV/PDF/JSON handling.
controls.limitations: No renderer, headers or output fixtures exist.

controls.description: Business change and durable intent commit atomically; jobs retain logical identity, revalidate current authority, fence stale attempts and reconcile unknown external outcomes.
controls.limitations: Queue schema, concurrency behavior and recovery tests are absent.

controls.description: Administrative changes atomically record append-only audit events; the security stream is closed, bounded and redacted, while emission, persistence and delivery remain distinct claims.
controls.limitations: OD-001 through OD-005 block parts of destination, retention, durability and AI-digest enforcement; no runtime coverage.

requirements.statement: The release provides a private web application and private API with the same company scope, authorization, validation and content restrictions.
OIDC user/admin roles and personal ownership boundaries govern protected operations; public access and native passwords are excluded.
Repository analysis is read-only except controlled system-owned issue writes, uses immutable evidence, reports gaps and stops on revoked authorization.
Authorized PDF, CSV and JSON exports preserve structured evidence, status, attribution, revision and export time.
Only approved enabled sources may be retrieved and retained with permission, provenance, immutable revisions, validation and visible failures.
External notifications and issues minimize private detail, recheck destination authority, preserve corrections and distinguish provider acceptance from readership.
Durable work survives restarts, preserves event identity, bounds retries and side effects, and exposes progress/failures.
requirements.origin: REQUIREMENTS.md FR-3.19 through FR-3.23, FR-6.7 and NFR-1

requirements.statement: External AI is optional, tool-less and advisory, receives only approved reduced input, and cannot relax local disclosure or matching authority.
Required actions record trusted actor/service, action, time, target, outcome and safe reason under the closed event contract and atomic audit rules.

risks.rationale: No caller-supplied risk rubric or sufficient rating inputs were provided; scenario confidence is not severity or probability.
risks.uncertainty: All threats are specification-grounded design hypotheses without implementation or runtime evidence.

coverage.reason: All five caller-named specifications and the caller scope statement were inventoried; unavailable implementation and technology-pack inputs are explicit.
No prior model, rubric or method fragment was supplied.
Stage 00 does not reconstruct the system; stage 01 will consume this context.
No optional branded method was requested or executed.
Threat analysis belongs to stage 02.
Control modeling belongs to stages 01 through 04.
Requirement mapping belongs to later stages.
No caller risk rubric was supplied and rating belongs to later stages.
Attack structures belong to stage 02 when evidence supports them.
Attack paths belong to stage 02 when evidence supports them.
Visualizations belong to stage 01 or later.
No conflicting source revisions were supplied; proposed versus required status is preserved as evidence limitations.
Evidence, topology, decision and technology gaps needed by later stages are recorded.
Treatment planning belongs to stage 04.
Verification planning belongs to stage 04; no tests ran.
Open decision subjects will be modeled in stage 04 without inventing owners or outcomes.
Stage 00 has no usable prior envelope, so no baseline delta declarations apply.
No prior model or method fragment identities were imported.
Browser, session, rendering, private-response and signout evidence questions were scoped; uploads, service workers and third-party scripts are absent release surfaces.
Caller, ownership, export, asynchronous authority, provider-response and destination evidence questions were scoped; inbound callbacks are absent for this release.
Actors, assets, data, zones, TB-1 through TB-10, principal flows, entry points, states and dependencies were reconstructed from specification claims and proposed-design premises.
Intended request, session and server use-case boundaries are modeled, but concrete routes and runtime enforcement are unavailable.
Rendering, no-store and authenticated-download requirements are modeled; browser/cache implementation evidence is unavailable.
The release defines no user file upload, preview or download object surface; repository content is provider ingestion, not a browser upload.
The proposed client uses bundled same-origin assets and the specifications prohibit remote resource loads; reassess if third-party browser code is introduced.
Global role and owner policies are modeled, but per-operation object/function/property rules are not enumerated.
Creation and retrieval are separate flows; retained-result lifetime and post-revocation authority remain open.
Outbound destination/result flow is modeled; inbound callbacks are not applicable, while returned-field business authority is a gap.
The existing architecture component diagram was used as evidence, but no new portable visualization record was necessary for this handoff.
Seventeen specification-grounded design hypotheses were developed; no evidenced weakness is claimed without implementation or execution observations.

The self-contained scenario baseline covered identity/session misuse, unauthorized changes, accountability, disclosure, resource exhaustion and privilege crossing without claiming an optional method execution.
T-001 traces ambient session authority to browser mutation; T-002 covers authority transitions. Required countercontrols and missing route/runtime evidence are explicit.
T-005 traces supplied untrusted content classes into user/admin views and preserves inert rendering requirements as counterevidence.
T-006 distinguishes shared cache/browser residual exposure from third-party transmission; third-party browser code remains not applicable.
T-003 and T-004 cover direct/alternate/delayed ownership and function/property authority, with the absent operation matrix preserved as a gap.
T-009, T-010 and T-015 analyze stale work, duplicate external effects and concurrent privileged configuration under supplied invariants.
T-007, T-008 and T-013 distinguish destination reachability, outbound disclosure and returned-field business authority.
FR-10.13 excludes inbound notification-provider callbacks and public webhooks; no separate external status feed is supplied.
All threats remain in one explicitly unrated risk record because no rubric or rating inputs were supplied.
No separate attack tree was needed; scenario prerequisites remain in stable threat records as the prompts require.
No separate graph was needed; flows, prerequisites and affected boundaries provide the supported paths without inventing state transitions.

gaps.description: No implementation, route/schema inventory, database schema, code, tests, runtime configuration, deployment evidence or observations exist.
gaps.needed: Implementation and verification evidence tied to each specified enforcement point.

gaps.description: The private API's concrete operations, resource/property policy and delayed-work authority handoff are not enumerated.
gaps.needed: API contract and use-case policy matrix with callers, roles, ownership, readable/writable properties, commitment points and revocation behavior.

gaps.description: The exact browser route and state-changing request inventory is absent.
gaps.needed: Route inventory mapping every cookie-authenticated mutation to intended authority, CSRF, origin and server operation checks.

gaps.description: Export creation, retained-result authorization, lifecycle and post-revocation retrieval are not fully allocated.
gaps.needed: End-to-end export lifecycle and component ownership contract for UI, API, worker, storage and download.

gaps.description: Provider response fields and the component authorized to translate each response into business state are not enumerated.
gaps.needed: Adapter response schemas, authority mapping and negative cases separate from provider acknowledgments.

gaps.description: Cache headers, browser storage and service-worker absence have no runtime evidence.
gaps.needed: Deployed response-header and browser-storage tests for private content and logout/session transitions.

gaps.description: OD-001 through OD-005 block security-event destination, retention, personal-data, durability and AI digest claims.
gaps.needed: Recorded decisions and independent verification evidence without inferring destinations or detectors.

gaps.description: DQ-8 does not define an exact typed confirmation target for every high-impact action.
gaps.needed: Design-owner mapping from each action to its visible exact confirmation value.

gaps.description: No exact resolved secure-coding technology pack was supplied.
gaps.needed: Resolver provenance for the selected stack if technology-specific prescriptions beyond the specifications are required.

changes.rationale: Stage 02 added supported design hypotheses across the composed web/API model without asserting implementation weaknesses.
Existing claimed controls now reference the threats they may mitigate; their implementation/test status is unchanged.
Stage 02 explicitly records that no risk rating is supported without a caller rubric and inputs.
Stage 02 records performed baseline/web/API lenses, the not-applicable callback surface and omitted optional graph structures.
